content.text: The `connect` handler lets a Worker accept raw socket connections, not just HTTP requests. You export `connect(socket, env, ctx)` next to `fetch`, and each incoming connection is passed to it as a socket you can read from and write to. Wrangler added this in 4.125.0, and you have 4.148.0 installed. To turn it on, add a top-level `connect` array to your wrangler config. Each entry opens a listening socket and needs `protocol: "tcp"` and a `port`, for example `"connect": [{ "protocol": "tcp", "port": 9000 }]` in `wrangler.jsonc`. You can also set `address`, which defaults to `127.0.0.1`. When you run `wrangler dev`, connections to that port go to your handler. Named environments don't inherit `connect`, so you have to repeat it in each `env.*` block. Your installed `config-schema.json` also accepts a `udp` variant with an `idle_timeout_ms` option, but the lesson only covers TCP, so I'd test UDP before relying on it.
